sentences.text:
Heard Sri Aadesh Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Utsav,
learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned Additional Government Advocate for the State.

2. This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.01 of 2022, under Sections 420, 466, 467, 468, 471,
409, 201 I.P.C., Police Station- Bargarh, District- Chitrakoot.
3. As per FIR, allegation against the applicant is that the applicant along with five other accused persons have manipulated the documents and also disappeared the Government records.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case just to harass the applicant.
He submitted that the charges levelled against the applicant is of the year 2015-16 wherein the applicant was initially appointed on the post of Gram Panchayat Adhikari.
He further submitted that investigation is going on and till date no charge sheet has been submitted against the applicant.
5. Sri Utsav, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 prays for and is granted two weeks time to file counter affidavit.

6. List and connect with Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No. 12244 of 2023 on 20.12.2023.
7.

4. Thereafter on 12.02.2024, following order was passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court:-
" 1. List revised.

2. Heard Sri P. K. Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Utsav, learned counsel for the first informant, Sri Bare Lal Bind, learned counsel for the State and perused the record.
3.
Learned counsel for the complainant/informant submits that he has filed his vakalatnama on behalf of the complainant/informant in the office on 09.1.2024.
The same is not on record.
Office to trace it out and place it on the record by the next date.
4. Learned counsel for the complainant/informant further prays for 3 weeks' time to file counter affidavit.
Prayer is allowed.
5. The applicant will have 10 days' thereafter to file rejoinder affidavit, if any.

"1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No. 01 of 2022, under Sections 420, 466, 467, 468, 471, 409, 201 IPC, Police Station- Bargarh, District- Chitrakoot.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.

He next submitted that the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 12.02.2024 granted interim anticipatory bail to the applicant till submission of the police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. Applicant has not misused the interim anticipatory bail granted to him and co-operated in the investigation proceedings.
He further submitted that in case applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.

4. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and has submitted that Investigating Officer after collecting evidence,
submitted charge-sheet against the applicant, as such, prima facie offence is made out against the applicant.
Hence, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant may be rejected.

5. Without expressing any opinion on merits of the case and considering the submissions advanced by counsel for the parties, the nature and gravity of the accusation, I find no good ground for anticipatory bail to the applicant in the aforesaid case.
6. Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is rejected.

7. However, if the applicant surrenders before the concerned court within one month from today and applies for bail, the bail application of the applicant shall be decided expeditiously by the court concerned, in accordance with law.
8. For the period of one month from today or till the time of surrender of the applicant before the Court below, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against him."
6. Learned counsel for the applicant challenged the order dated 02.05.2024 before the Hon'ble Apex Court by filing Criminal Appeal No.3315 of 2024 arising out of S.L.P. No.6940 of 2024.
The Hon'ble Apex Court vide order dated 09.08.2024 set aside the impugned orders passed by this Court and remand the matter.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
Lastly, it is submitted that the applicant is apprehensive of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.

8. Learned AGA has filed a counter affidavit dated 11.11.2025 in which paragraph no.8 clearly states that up till now, charge sheet has not been submitted before this Court and the investigation is pending against the applicant.
